LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 WORD CLASS: ADJECTIVES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we compare things, people or events?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text
2. order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately
3. use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 WORD CLASS: ADJECTIVES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 WORD CLASS: ADJECTIVES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately

What this means
In this part you learn to order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately

What this means
In this part you learn to use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives to a partner. (skill: order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text.
3. Practise this skill: order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately.
4. Practise this skill: use the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives accurately.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we compare things, people or events?
2. Which words are used to describe things or people?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in a text.
5. Be able to: order adjectives in terms of size, shape and age appropriately.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
